topic: 924 Sanad offices. All staffed by Omani nationals. All serving every company in the country. The ones that digitise their operations first will take the market — the rest will lose clients to them.
format: Open with a number that puts the problem in scale — 924 offices, 40 permits, 15 visa renewals, 200 filings per month — then show what managing that volume without a system actually looks like
post:
40 work permits. 15 visa renewals. 8 MOL filings. 20 client companies.

That's a quiet Tuesday for most Sanad offices in Oman.

Now picture tracking all of it through a WhatsApp group that hasn't been read since yesterday, an Excel sheet three people have edited differently, and a handwritten register that only makes sense to the person who wrote it.

That's not a process. That's a memory game — and someone always loses.

There are 924 licensed Sanad offices across Oman. Every one of them staffed by Omani nationals. Every one of them the legal gateway for every company in the country that needs a work permit, residency visa, MOL filing, or civil status transaction done correctly.

The offices that build a real system this year — structured cases, expiry alerts, client portals, automated invoicing — will absorb clients from the ones still running on screenshots.

Not because they're bigger. Because they're easier to trust.

Work permit tracking in Oman shouldn't depend on who's in the office that morning.

Which part of your current process would break first if your best PRO officer called in sick today?
